instructions.name: cancel_agreement_reconciled
docs: v2.1: single-transaction, Kamino-aware `cancel_agreement`. Redeems the
full `escrow_kamino_collateral` balance (if any) back into
`escrow_usdc` first, then runs the same fee/refund split
`cancel_agreement` does — so a buyer never needs to know a separate
`kamino_probe_redeem` crank exists before they can cancel cleanly.
Purely additive: `cancel_agreement` is untouched, and this degrades to
the same behavior when an agreement never touched Kamino. See
`cancel_agreement_reconciled.rs`.

accounts.name: merchant_usdc
docs: Cancellation-fee destination — must belong to the recorded merchant so
the buyer cannot route the fee back to themselves (see cancel_agreement.rs).

docs: See kamino_probe.rs — governance-approved Kamino target set.

accounts.name: kamino_program

accounts.name: escrow_kamino_collateral
docs: `init_if_needed`, same as `kamino_probe`'s collateral account: an
agreement that never touched Kamino has no `escrow_kamino_collateral`
account yet. This is what lets the instruction degrade to plain
`cancel_agreement` — the account is created with a zero balance (so
`collateral_balance == 0`, the reconcile branch is skipped) rather
than the whole call reverting.

instructions.name: create_agent_mandate
docs: Owner lets one agent buy on their behalf inside `limits`, and
delegates a bounded USDC allowance to the mandate PDA.

accounts.name: merchant
docs: Not a signer; merchant is only needed at withdrawal time.

accounts.name: protocol_config
docs: Constant PDA seed — no other account/instruction-arg dependency — so
Anchor's TS client auto-derives and injects this address even when
callers never list it in `.accounts()`. Deliberately `UncheckedAccount`,
not `Account<ProtocolConfig>`: the PDA may not exist yet (pre-governance
deployments, or any caller who hasn't called `init_protocol_config`),
and an `Account<T>` wrapper would hard-fail deserialization in that
case. The handler manually checks ownership and treats a
system-owned (uninitialized) account as "no risk controls configured."
`mut` so `apply_tvl_increase` can write the updated `current_tvl` back
(a no-op write when the PDA is uninitialized — see protocol_config.rs).

instructions.name: create_agreement_kamino
docs: v2.1: `create_agreement` plus an inline Kamino deposit of the first
installment (same fallback rules as `pay_installment_kamino`).
Purely additive; see `create_agreement_kamino.rs`.

instructions.name: init_kamino_config
docs: Creates the singleton KaminoConfig PDA. Caller becomes governance authority.

accounts.name: upgrade_authority
docs: Only the program's upgrade authority (the deployer) may create this
singleton. Without this gate the first caller after deploy would
become governance and could point every escrow's Kamino CPI (signed
by the agreement PDA) at a program of their choosing.

instructions.name: init_protocol_config
docs: Creates the singleton ProtocolConfig PDA. Caller becomes governance authority.

accounts.name: upgrade_authority
docs: Only the program's upgrade authority (the deployer) may create this
singleton. Without this gate the first caller after deploy would
become governance and could pause the protocol or set a TVL cap that
blocks every deposit.

instructions.name: kamino_probe_deposit
docs: Moves USDC already sitting in an agreement's escrow into a Kamino
(or mock-Kamino) reserve. Never fails the transaction on a CPI
error — emits a fallback event instead.

instructions.name: merchant_withdraw_reconciled
docs: v2.1: single-transaction, Kamino-aware `merchant_withdraw`. If
`escrow_usdc` alone doesn't cover `total_price`, redeems just enough
`escrow_kamino_collateral` first (same CPI path as
`kamino_probe_redeem`), then pays the merchant — collapsing the
previous two-transaction "crank, then withdraw" flow into one. Purely
additive: `merchant_withdraw` is untouched, and this degrades to the
same behavior when an agreement never touched Kamino. See
`merchant_withdraw_reconciled.rs`.

accounts.name: merchant_usdc
docs: The payout destination doubles as the authorization check — must be
owned by `agreement.merchant`, same constraint `merchant_withdraw`
uses (there it's expressed via a `Signer` + key-match; here there's
no dedicated merchant signer since any keeper may submit the tx).

accounts.name: escrow_kamino_collateral

agreement that never touched Kamino has no `escrow_kamino_collateral`
account yet, and `Account<'info, TokenAccount>` deserialization would
fail outright on a missing account before the handler ever runs. This
is what lets the instruction degrade to plain `merchant_withdraw` —
the account is created with a zero balance (so `collateral_balance ==
0`, the reconcile branch is skipped) rather than the whole call
reverting.

this signer, is what's authorization-checked.

types.name: AgentMandate
docs: Agent BNPL: what an owner lets one AI agent buy on their behalf.
PDA seeds: ["agent_mandate", owner, agent]. The owner keeps custody: USDC
stays in the owner's own token account, which delegates a bounded SPL
allowance to this PDA. The mandate spends only from that bound account;
revoke accepts any owner token account. Agreements record `buyer = owner`, so
repayment, cancellation and default work exactly as for any other
agreement.

types.name: KaminoConfig
docs: v2.1: landing pad for real Kamino Lend CPI (DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md v2.1
items 1-3). See `docs/design/KAMINO_CPI_INTEGRATION.md` for the full
technical design (verified against Kamino's actual source, fetched
2026-07-14) — account layout for `deposit_reserve_liquidity` /
`redeem_reserve_collateral`, the anchor-lang version-mismatch risk
(0.32.1 here vs 0.29.0 in klend, meaning we can't use their typed
`Program<'info, _>` wrappers and must build the CPI instruction
manually), and why a cloned-devnet-market localnet test can't validate
a real deposit (oracle staleness).
A singleton governance PDA (seeds = ["kamino_config"]), mirroring the
exact `ProtocolConfig` pattern already used in this codebase: shipped
ahead of the CPI code that will consume it, `enabled` defaults to
`false` so an uninitialized or disabled config is a pure no-op and
every code path today (raw-USDC escrow, simulated yield) is completely
unaffected. No instruction reads this account yet — it exists so the
next session's CPI call has a concrete place to source its target
reserve/market accounts from, set once via governance instead of
hardcoded per-instruction.

types.name: MandateLimits
docs: Owner-chosen limits, shared by create and update.

types.name: ProtocolConfig
docs: v2.1: protocol-wide risk controls, laid down ahead of real Kamino CPI
yield (see DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md v2.1 item 5). A singleton PDA
(seeds = ["protocol_config"]) governing an emergency pause switch and
deposit/TVL caps.
Wired into `create_agreement` and `pay_installment` as a constant-seed PDA
account (`UncheckedAccount`, no client-side change needed — Anchor's TS
client auto-derives constant-seed PDAs even when the caller's
`.accounts()` never mentions them, which is what keeps the frozen v1
characterization suite untouched). `create_agreement` enforces `paused`
and `max_agreement_deposit` (against `total_price`, the agreement's
maximum ever exposure); `pay_installment` enforces `paused` on every
subsequent payment too, so an emergency pause halts USDC moving into
escrow on existing agreements, not just new agreement creation. An
uninitialized (system-owned) PDA is treated as "no risk controls
configured."
`tvl_cap` / `current_tvl` are now enforced end-to-end: every path that
moves money in or out of escrow (create_agreement, pay_installment,
merchant_withdraw, cancel_agreement, trigger_default) calls
`apply_tvl_increase`/`apply_tvl_decrease` (protocol_config.rs) to keep
`current_tvl` accurate and reject deposits that would breach `tvl_cap`.
Not yet wired into `stake_usdc` (stake pool deposits are a separate token
flow from BNPL escrow TVL). Real Kamino CPI (v2.1 items 1-3) will need to
touch these same call sites again when escrow moves from raw USDC to
kTokens, but the bookkeeping itself no longer waits on that work.
